mechanism_narrative: The recent decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT together with rising RESIDENTIAL implies weaker daily out-of-home activity, which should continue to suppress retail visits and keep RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above the last 28-day mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover from their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: If residential time keeps falling from its elevated level, that signals more time spent outside home and more discretionary shopping trips, which raises RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 18 points after having stayed above 19 points for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: A further drop in RESIDENTIAL below 18 is not followed by any increase in RETAIL_REC within the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases commuting-linked retail stopovers, so when both series improve together retail-and-recreation mobility rises over the following four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve together for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the subsequent 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When transit mobility is stuck near a deep trough, access friction persists and retail recovery stalls; only a sustained TRANSIT rebound should lift RETAIL_REC, so current transit weakness predicts lower retail mobility over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70 for at least three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT stays below -70 for three weeks but RETAIL_REC nevertheless rises above its previous four-week mean within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in PARKS mobility can displace some discretionary time from outdoor recreation back into nearby shopping trips when weather and leisure demand normalize, producing a short-run rise in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: A week-on-week PARKS increase of more than 5 points is not followed by any RETAIL_REC increase in the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both rise while RESIDENTIAL falls, households are reallocating time from home into essential and discretionary errands, and that combined trip normalization should push retail mobility higher over four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both rise while RESIDENTIAL falls, yet RETAIL_REC does not stay above its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES keeps improving from its current low level and TRANSIT does not deteriorate further, commuting confidence returns and retail mobility follows with a two-week lag.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 2 points week-on-week while TRANSIT is flat or improving
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by at least 2 points week-on-week with TRANSIT flat or better, but RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a restrictions-easing regime, broad recovery in mobility outside the home should translate into retail gains; a simultaneous rise in PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES indicates that consumers are moving more across the city, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next month.
failure_condition: PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all improve together but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 28-day mean within 28 days.
